# Introduction

(In the spirit of Advent of Code, if not actually advent-of-code problems because the license doesn't allow that). 

You're in charge of logistics and predictive analytics for Santa's workshop at the North Pole. 
There have been some supply chain issues this year that mean that the workshop hasn't been able to obtain the parts necessary to build enough of some popular toys. 
It's important to figure out which toys are impacted, identify demand for those toys, and determine what alternative presents each child should receive. 

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)
library(ggplot2)
library(readxl)

if (!file.exists("Toys.xlsx")) {
  download.file("https://github.com/unl-statistics/stat850/raw/refs/heads/main/exams/final/Toys.xlsx", "Toys.xlsx")
}
toys <- read_xlsx("Toys.xlsx", sheet = 1)
wishlist <- read_xlsx("Toys.xlsx", sheet = 2)
```


# Affected Toys


## Electrical regulators

One of the parts which is hard to acquire this year is an electrical regulator that modulates between the battery 🔋 and a circuit board to ensure that the circuit board doesn't short out ⚡. 
All of these parts have been gobbled up by computer chip manufacturers to build AI data centers 😢. 

Identify the toys which may be impacted by this shortage (toys with chips and batteries). Output a table with the toy name and relative demand, sorted in decreasing order by demand. 

Your table should be nicely formatted using a function such as `knitr::kable`, `DT:DT`, etc.

There is also a shortage of fabric, since JoAnn fabrics went out of business (they were the North Pole's #1 fabric supplier).
